verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः |
स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
anāśritaḥ karmaphalaṃ kāryaṃ karma karoti yaḥ |
sa saṃnyāsī ca yogī ca na niragnirna cākriyaḥ || 1 ||
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: One who performs prescribed duty without depending on the fruits of action is a true renunciant (Sannyasi) and a true yogi; not one who merely abandons the sacred fire or ceases all work.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna begins by dismantling the misconception that spirituality means running away from practical responsibility. Merely discarding social rituals or abandoning physical work does not make one a yogi. True renunciation is internal detachment while diligently performing one's duties.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव |
न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
yaṃ saṃnyāsamiti prāhuryogaṃ taṃ viddhi pāṇḍava |
na hyasaṃnyastasaṅkalpo yogī bhavati kaścana || 2 ||
verses.translation: Know that which is called renunciation (Sannyasa) to be identical with Yoga, O Pandava. For no one can become a true yogi without renouncing selfish motive and desire-prompted intention (Sankalpa).
verses.meaning: Sannyasa and Yoga converge in purpose. A person cannot master the mind in meditation while still nursing egoic cravings and future calculations. Renouncing selfish intent is the prerequisite for meditative stillness.

verses.text_sanskrit:
आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते |
योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
ārurukṣormuneryogaṃ karma kāraṇamucyate |
yogārūḍhasya tasyaiva śamaḥ kāraṇamucyate || 3 ||
verses.translation: For an aspirant who seeks to ascend the heights of Yoga (Arurukshu), selfless action is said to be the means. For one who has ascended to the summit of Yoga (Yogarudha), serene tranquility (Shama) is said to be the means.
verses.meaning: The path of spiritual ascent has two stages: active selfless service (Karma Yoga) cleanses the subconscious mind for beginners, while effortless stillness and meditative tranquility (Shama) sustain the advanced master.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते |
सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
yadā hi nendriyārtheṣu na karmasvanuṣajjate |
sarvasaṅkalpasaṃnyāsī yogārūḍhastadocyate || 4 ||
verses.translation: When a person is no longer attached to sense objects or to fruitive actions, having completely renounced all selfish thoughts and desires, that person is said to be established in Yoga (Yogarudha).
verses.meaning: The state of Yogarudha is defined: complete psychological freedom from sensory craving and egoic ambition. The mind rests undisturbed in transcendental equilibrium.

verses.text_sanskrit:
उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् |
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
uddharedātmanātmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet |
ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ || 5 ||
verses.translation: One must elevate oneself by one's own mind, and never degrade oneself. For the mind alone is one's friend, and the mind alone is one's enemy.
verses.meaning: One of the most empowering verses in world philosophy: You are your own ultimate savior or destroyer. An undisciplined, reactive mind acts as a treacherous internal adversary, while a trained, spiritualized mind becomes your most steadfast and loyal friend.

verses.text_sanskrit:
बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः |
अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
bandhurātmātmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ |
anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat || 6 ||
verses.translation: For one who has conquered the lower self (the senses and mind) through the higher Self, the mind is a benevolent friend. But for one who has failed to do so, the mind remains a hostile enemy.
verses.meaning: Inner victory is the true test of human strength. When the mind is subordinated to the discriminating intellect and the immortal Atman, it works in total harmony with your spiritual purpose.

verses.text_sanskrit:
जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः |
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
jitātmanaḥ praśāntasya paramātmā samāhitaḥ |
śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu tathā mānāpamānayoḥ || 7 ||
verses.translation: For one who has mastered the self and attained deep tranquility, the Supreme Self is constantly realized in profound absorption, remaining unaffected by cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honor and dishonor.
verses.meaning: Equanimity across all pairs of worldly opposites (Dvandvas) allows the direct, uninterrupted experience of the Supreme Spirit (Paramatman) within one's own heart.

verses.text_sanskrit:
ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः |
युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
jñānavijñānatṛptātmā kūṭastho vijitendriyaḥ |
yukta ityucyate yogī samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ || 8 ||
verses.translation: The yogi who is fully satisfied with scriptural knowledge (Jnana) and direct realization (Vijnana), who is unshakeable like a rock (Kutastha), whose senses are mastered, and to whom a lump of earth, a stone, and gold are equal—that person is said to be truly united in Yoga.
verses.meaning: Theoretical learning transforms into experiential wisdom (Vijnana). Rooted in the immortal Soul, the yogi is free from materialism, seeing no intrinsic spiritual difference between a clod of clay and pure gold.

verses.text_sanskrit:
सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु |
साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
suhṛnmitrāryudāsīnamadhyasthadveṣyabandhuṣu |
sādhuṣvapi ca pāpeṣu samabuddhirviśiṣyate || 9 ||
verses.translation: One who regards with equal vision the well-wisher, the friend, the foe, the neutral arbiter, the mediator, the hateful, the relative, and equally the saint and the sinner—that person is regarded as foremost among all.
verses.meaning: Universal compassion and unconditional fairness: The perfected seer does not view people through the distorted lens of prejudice, personal benefit, or resentment, but perceives the same divine consciousness in all.

verses.text_sanskrit:
योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः |
एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
yogī yuñjīta satatamātmānaṃ rahasi sthitaḥ |
ekākī yatacittātmā nirāśīraparigrahaḥ || 10 ||
verses.translation: The yogi should constantly concentrate the mind upon the Supreme, remaining in seclusion, alone, with mind and body controlled, free from desire and possessiveness.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna begins laying out the practical discipline of Dhyana Yoga. Regular periods of solitude, free from distractions, cravings, and excessive possessions, provide the sacred sanctuary for profound communion.

verses.text_sanskrit:
शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः |
नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरम् || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiramāsanamātmanaḥ |
nātyucchritaṃ nātinīcaṃ cailājinakuśottaram || 11 ||
verses.translation: In a clean, sanctified place, one should establish a firm meditation seat, neither too high nor too low, covered successively with sacred Kusha grass, a deerskin, and a soft cloth.
verses.meaning: Practical ergonomics and atmospheric purity for meditation. A clean environment and a stable, comfortable seat prevent restlessness, ground subtle energies, and support prolonged spiritual focus.

verses.text_sanskrit:
तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः |
उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
tatraikāgraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yatacittendriyakriyaḥ |
upaviśyāsane yuñjyādyogamātmaviśuddhaye || 12 ||
verses.translation: Sitting upon that seat, making the mind one-pointed, controlling the thoughts and the activities of the senses, one should practice Yoga for the purification of the inner self.
verses.meaning: The fundamental technique: gathering the scattered rays of the wandering mind into a single laser-like focus (Ekagra) to cleanse the mirror of consciousness (Atma-vishuddhaye).

verses.text_sanskrit:
समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः |
सम्प्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन् || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
samaṃ kāyaśirogrīvaṃ dhārayannacalaṃ sthiraḥ |
samprekṣya nāsikāgraṃ svaṃ diśaścānavalokayan || 13 ||
verses.translation: Holding the torso, head, and neck erect in a straight line, motionless and steady, gazing gently at the tip of one's nose without looking around in other directions...
verses.meaning: The physical posture (Asana) of meditation: an aligned, erect spinal column facilitates the unobstructed flow of vital energy (Prana), while an unfocused, gentle forward gaze (Nasikagra Drishti) quiets optic nerve stimulation and calms thought waves.

verses.text_sanskrit:
प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः |
मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
praśāntātmā vigatabhīrbrahmacārivrate sthitaḥ |
manaḥ saṃyamya maccitto yukta āsīta matparaḥ || 14 ||
verses.translation: ...serene in soul, fearless, steadfast in the vow of Brahmacharya (purity), controlling the mind, fixing all thoughts on Me, the practitioner should sit in meditation, with Me as the supreme goal.
verses.meaning: The inner psychological disposition for meditation: complete fearlessness (Vigatabhi), moral integrity and purity of energy (Brahmacharya), and devotional absorption in Sri Krishna as the ultimate destination.

verses.text_sanskrit:
युञ्जन्नेवं सदात्मानं योगी नियतमानसः |
शान्तिं निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
yuñjannevaṃ sadātmānaṃ yogī niyatamānasaḥ |
śāntiṃ nirvāṇaparamāṃ matsaṃsthāmadhigacchati || 15 ||
verses.translation: Constantly training and harmonizing the mind in this manner, the yogi of disciplined consciousness attains supreme peace—the liberation (Nirvana) that abides in Me.
verses.meaning: The fruit of regular, dedicated meditation: deep transcendental peace culminating in supreme liberation (Nirvana-parama), which is eternally established in the Divine consciousness of Sri Krishna.

verses.text_sanskrit:
नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः |
न चाति स्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
nātyaśnatastu yogo'sti na caikāntamanaśnataḥ |
na cāti svapnaśīlasya jāgrato naiva cārjuna || 16 ||
verses.translation: Yoga is not possible for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all; nor is it possible, O Arjuna, for one who sleeps too much or one who stays awake excessively.
verses.meaning: The Golden Mean of spiritual life: Sri Krishna rejects extreme ascetic mortification as well as hedonistic overindulgence. Extremes unbalance the nervous system; spiritual mastery flourishes in balanced moderation.

verses.text_sanskrit:
युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु |
युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
yuktāhāravihārasya yuktaceṣṭasya karmasu |
yuktasvapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkhahā || 17 ||
verses.translation: For one who is temperate in eating and recreation, disciplined in all actions of work, and regulated in sleep and wakefulness, Yoga becomes the destroyer of all sorrows (Duhkha-ha).
verses.meaning: A masterpiece on holistic wellness: Harmony in diet, wholesome recreation, disciplined work, and rhythmic sleep transforms Yoga into an all-encompassing antidote to human stress and suffering.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते |
निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
yadā viniyataṃ cittamātmanyevāvatiṣṭhate |
niḥspṛhaḥ sarvakāmebhyo yukta ityucyate tadā || 18 ||
verses.translation: When the fully restrained and purified mind rests securely in the Self alone, completely free from all cravings and desires, then a person is said to be established in Yoga (Yukta).
verses.meaning: True meditation is not empty void, but rich inner fullness. When the mind rests joyfully in the immortal Atman, external cravings naturally drop away like dry leaves.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता |
योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
yathā dīpo nivātastho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā |
yogino yatacittasya yuñjato yogamātmanaḥ || 19 ||
verses.translation: As a flame of a lamp in a windless place does not flicker, such is the traditional analogy used for the disciplined mind of a yogi absorbed in meditation on the Self.
verses.meaning: One of the most poetic and timeless metaphors in spiritual literature: In a sheltered room, the oil lamp flame burns perfectly straight, bright, and motionless. Even so, the yogi's mind in meditation burns with steady, unswerving spiritual radiance.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया |
यत्र चैवात्मनात्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
yatroparamate cittaṃ niruddhaṃ yogasevayā |
yatra caivātmanātmānaṃ paśyannātmani tuṣyati || 20 ||
verses.translation: That state in which the mind, restrained by the practice of Yoga, attains absolute stillness, and in which, perceiving the Self through the purified inner self, one rejoices in the Self alone...
verses.meaning: The beginning of Sri Krishna's description of Samadhi: The mind becomes utterly tranquil, and the soul discovers unconditional, self-contained bliss within its own divine essence.

verses.text_sanskrit:
सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद्बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् |
वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः || २१ ||
verses.transliteration:
sukhamātyantikaṃ yattadbuddhigrāhyamatīndriyam |
vetti yatra na caivāyaṃ sthitaścalati tattvataḥ || 21 ||
verses.translation: ...wherein one experiences that boundless, transcendental bliss which is grasped by the purified intellect beyond the reach of the physical senses; established in which, one never departs from the ultimate truth...
verses.meaning: The bliss of Self-realization (Atyantika Sukham) is infinitely sweeter than all sensory pleasures combined. Once rooted in this sublime reality, the seeker is never again deceived by worldly illusions.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः |
यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते || २२ ||
verses.transliteration:
yaṃ labdhvā cāparaṃ lābhaṃ manyate nādhikaṃ tataḥ |
yasminsthito na duḥkhena guruṇāpi vicālyate || 22 ||
verses.translation: ...having attained which, one regards no other gain as superior; and established in which, one is not shaken even by the heaviest and most grievous sorrow...
verses.meaning: The ultimate spiritual security: In this exalted state of consciousness, no worldly treasure can compare to what is found within, and no external catastrophe or sorrow (even death of loved ones) can disturb one's inner peace.

verses.text_sanskrit:
तं विद्याद्दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसञ्ज्ञितम् |
स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा || २३ ||
verses.transliteration:
taṃ vidyādduḥkhasaṃyogaviyogaṃ yogasañjñitam |
sa niścayena yoktavyo yogo'nirviṇṇacetasā || 23 ||
verses.translation: Know that state of severance from all union with pain and suffering to be called Yoga. This Yoga must be practiced with firm determination and with an unwearied, patient heart.
verses.meaning: A profound redefinition of Yoga: it is the total disconnection from sorrow (Duhkha-samyoga-viyogam). Success requires unshakable resolve (Nishchaya) and cheerful perseverance without despondency (Anirvinna-chetasa).

verses.text_sanskrit:
सङ्कल्पप्रभवान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषतः |
मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः || २४ ||
verses.transliteration:
saṅkalpaprabhavānkāmāṃstyaktvā sarvānaśeṣataḥ |
manasaivendriyagrāmaṃ viniyamya samantataḥ || 24 ||
verses.translation: Completely renouncing all desires born of imagination and personal ambition, and restraining the entire assembly of senses from all sides by the power of the mind alone...
verses.meaning: Desires originate from mental visualization and daydreaming (Sankalpa). Cutting desire at its root by silencing mental chatter allows total mastery over sensory inputs.

verses.text_sanskrit:
शनैः शनैरुपरमेद्बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया |
आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् || २५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śanaiḥ śanairuparamedbuddhyā dhṛtigṛhītayā |
ātmasaṃsthaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiñcidapi cintayet || 25 ||
verses.translation: Gradually, step by step, one should quiet the mind through the intellect guided by steadfast fortitude; anchoring the mind firmly in the Self, one should think of nothing else.
verses.meaning: The art of gentle meditation: Never fight the mind violently. Gradually and patiently ('Shanaih shanaih'), using patient willpower (Dhriti), guide the thoughts to rest peacefully in the silent sanctuary of the Self.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् |
ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् || २६ ||
verses.transliteration:
yato yato niścarati manaścañcalamasthiram |
tatastato niyamyaitadātmanyeva vaśaṃ nayet || 26 ||
verses.translation: From whatever cause the restless and unsteady mind wanders away, one should gently withdraw it from that and bring it back under the control of the Self alone.
verses.meaning: The universal meditation instruction: It is the natural habit of the untrained mind to wander. Whenever you notice the mind straying toward memories, anxieties, or fantasies, without self-criticism, gently and repeatedly bring it back to the present presence of the Soul.

verses.text_sanskrit:
प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम् |
उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम् || २७ ||
verses.transliteration:
praśāntamanasaṃ hyenaṃ yoginaṃ sukhamuttamam |
upaiti śāntarajasaṃ brahmabhūtamakalmaṣam || 27 ||
verses.translation: Supreme bliss naturally comes to this yogi whose mind is perfectly tranquil, whose passions are fully pacified, who is free from all blemishes, and who has attained oneness with Brahman.
verses.meaning: When the turbulence of passion (Rajas) subsides, the mind becomes an undisturbed mirror reflecting the unalloyed, supreme bliss of Brahman.

verses.text_sanskrit:
युञ्जन्नेवं सदात्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः |
सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते || २८ ||
verses.transliteration:
yuñjannevaṃ sadātmānaṃ yogī vigatakalmaṣaḥ |
sukhena brahmasaṃsparśamatyantaṃ sukhamaśnute || 28 ||
verses.translation: The yogi, cleansed of all impurities, constantly engaging the self in Yoga, easily and effortlessly experiences the infinite bliss of intimate contact with the Supreme Brahman (Brahma-samsparsha).
verses.meaning: Meditation becomes effortless and joyful (Sukhena). The soul experiences 'Brahma-samsparsha'—the direct, living touch of the Infinite Divine, bestowing boundless, eternal happiness.

verses.text_sanskrit:
सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि |
ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः || २९ ||
verses.transliteration:
sarvabhūtasthamātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani |
īkṣate yogayuktātmā sarvatra samadarśanaḥ || 29 ||
verses.translation: One whose consciousness is unified in Yoga perceives the Self residing in all living beings, and all beings abiding in the Self, beholding the same Divine everywhere with equal vision.
verses.meaning: The expansive vision of the mystic: The walls of individuality dissolve. The yogi sees the one eternal consciousness permeating all creation, and all of creation nested within the infinite expanse of the Divine.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति |
तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति || ३० ||
verses.transliteration:
yo māṃ paśyati sarvatra sarvaṃ ca mayi paśyati |
tasyāhaṃ na praṇaśyāmi sa ca me na praṇaśyati || 30 ||
verses.translation: For one who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me, I am never lost to that person, nor is that person ever lost to Me.
verses.meaning: One of the most tender, comforting promises in the Bhagavad Gita. When a devotee sees Sri Krishna's divine presence in all aspects of life, an eternal, unbreakable bond of mutual love and protection is forged with the Supreme.

verses.text_sanskrit:
सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः |
सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते || ३१ ||
verses.transliteration:
sarvabhūtasthitaṃ yo māṃ bhajatyekatvamāsthitaḥ |
sarvathā vartamāno'pi sa yogī mayi vartate || 31 ||
verses.translation: The yogi who, established in oneness, worships Me as dwelling within all living beings—in whatever way that person lives and acts, that yogi continually abides in Me.
verses.meaning: True devotion transcends temples and rituals: seeing God in every living soul and serving life with love is the highest worship. Such a yogi lives forever in divine communion, regardless of external circumstances.

verses.text_sanskrit:
आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन |
सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं स योगी परमो मतः || ३२ ||
verses.transliteration:
ātmaupamyena sarvatra samaṃ paśyati yo'rjuna |
sukhaṃ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṃ sa yogī paramo mataḥ || 32 ||
verses.translation: One who, by comparison with oneself, sees the joy and sorrow of all living beings as identical to one's own, O Arjuna—that person is regarded as the highest yogi.
verses.meaning: The Golden Rule of empathy and cosmic oneness (Atmaupamya): Feeling another's suffering as your own and rejoicing in another's happiness as your own is declared by Sri Krishna to be the ultimate pinnacle of Yoga.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन |
एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात्स्थितिं स्थिराम् || ३३ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
yo'yaṃ yogastvayā proktaḥ sāmyena madhusūdana |
etasyāhaṃ na paśyāmi cañcalatvātsthitiṃ sthirām || 33 ||
verses.translation: Arjuna said: O Madhusudana, regarding this Yoga of equanimity which You have described, I do not see how it can have a permanent stability, owing to the restless nature of the human mind.
verses.meaning: Arjuna speaks for all struggling spiritual seekers: The vision of universal equanimity and unbroken stillness sounds sublime, but the turbulent nature of the mind makes it seem almost impossible to sustain.

verses.text_sanskrit:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् |
तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् || ३४ ||
verses.transliteration:
cañcalaṃ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa pramāthi balavaddṛḍham |
tasyāhaṃ nigrahaṃ manye vāyoriva suduṣkaram || 34 ||
verses.translation: For the mind is indeed restless, turbulent, obstinate, and extraordinarily powerful, O Krishna! To control it, I believe, is as difficult as curbing the raging wind.
verses.meaning: A vivid description of psychological turbulence: The mind is 'Chanchala' (fickle), 'Pramathi' (agitating), 'Balavat' (forceful), and 'Dridham' (stubborn). Controlling it feels as daunting as catching a hurricane in one's hands.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम् |
अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते || ३५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
asaṃśayaṃ mahābāho mano durnigrahaṃ calam |
abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa ca gṛhyate || 35 ||
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: Without doubt, O mighty-armed Arjuna, the mind is restless and difficult to curb. But by repeated practice (Abhyasa) and detachment (Vairagya), O son of Kunti, it can definitely be mastered.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna's famous twin formula for mind mastery: 1. Abhyasa (consistent, disciplined spiritual practice) and 2. Vairagya (cultivating dispassion and stepping back from worldly obsessions). With these two wings, the soul soars to peace.

verses.text_sanskrit:
असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः |
वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः || ३६ ||
verses.transliteration:
asaṃyatātmanā yogo duṣprāpa iti me matiḥ |
vaśyātmanā tu yatatā śakyo'vāptumupāyataḥ || 36 ||
verses.translation: Yoga is difficult to attain for one who is undisciplined in mind; this is My opinion. But for one whose self is controlled, striving through proper means, it can certainly be achieved.
verses.meaning: Spiritual success is not a matter of luck, but of systematic method (Upaya) and self-discipline. A sincere seeker who applies the right spiritual tools will inevitably triumph over the mind.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
अयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चचलितमानसः |
अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति || ३७ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
ayatiḥ śraddhayopeto yogāccalitamānasaḥ |
aprāpya yogasaṃsiddhiṃ kāṃ gatiṃ kṛṣṇa gacchati || 37 ||
verses.translation: Arjuna said: What is the fate of one who begins the spiritual path with faith, but whose mind wanders away due to lack of perseverance, failing to reach the perfection of Yoga, O Krishna?
verses.meaning: Arjuna expresses a universal anxiety: What happens to a sincere seeker who strives on the spiritual path but falls short or dies before achieving full enlightenment? Is all that spiritual effort wasted?

verses.text_sanskrit:
कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति |
अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि || ३८ ||
verses.transliteration:
kaccinnobhayavibhraṣṭaśchinnābhramiva naśyati |
apratiṣṭho mahābāho vimūḍho brahmaṇaḥ pathi || 38 ||
verses.translation: Fallen from both worldly success and spiritual perfection, without any foundation, deluded on the path to Brahman, does such a person not perish like a broken, scattered cloud, O mighty-armed Lord?
verses.meaning: Arjuna fears the tragic fate of being 'Ubhaya-vibhrashta'—giving up worldly pleasures on one hand, yet failing to attain God on the other, dissipating into nothingness like a torn cloud.

verses.text_sanskrit:
एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः |
त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते || ३९ ||
verses.transliteration:
etanme saṃśayaṃ kṛṣṇa chettumarhasyaśeṣataḥ |
tvadanyaḥ saṃśayasyāsya chettā na hyupapadyate || 39 ||
verses.translation: O Krishna, please dispel this doubt of mine completely; for there is none other to be found who is capable of dispelling this doubt except You!
verses.meaning: Arjuna surrenders his doubt to the omniscient Lord, acknowledging Sri Krishna as the sole master who can unveil the cosmic laws governing the destiny of the soul.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते |
न हि कल्याणकृत्कश्चिद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति || ४० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
pārtha naiveha nāmutra vināśastasya vidyate |
na hi kalyāṇakṛtkaściddurgatiṃ tāta gacchati || 40 ||
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: O Partha, neither in this world nor in the world to come is there any destruction for such a soul! For no one who does good, My dear friend, ever comes to an evil end.
verses.meaning: A monument of divine reassurance: No spiritual effort is ever lost in the cosmic ledger. Goodness and spiritual longing permanently enrich the soul. The Divine protects every step taken toward righteousness (Kalyana-krit).

verses.text_sanskrit:
प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः |
शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते || ४१ ||
verses.transliteration:
prāpya puṇyakṛtāṃ lokānuṣitvā śāśvatīḥ samāḥ |
śucīnāṃ śrīmatāṃ gehe yogabhraṣṭo'bhijāyate || 41 ||
verses.translation: Having attained the heavenly realms of the virtuous and dwelt there for countless years, one who fell from Yoga is reborn into a pious and prosperous family upon earth.
verses.meaning: The law of spiritual continuity: A seeker whose practice was interrupted enjoys celestial rest before taking rebirth in an auspicious, virtuous, and well-provided household where spiritual pursuits can easily resume.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अथ वा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम् |
एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम् || ४२ ||
verses.transliteration:
atha vā yogināmeva kule bhavati dhīmatām |
etaddhi durlabhataraṃ loke janma yadīdṛśam || 42 ||
verses.translation: Or such an advanced seeker is born directly into a family of wise and enlightened yogis. Such a birth in this world is exceedingly rare and blessed.
verses.meaning: For more advanced practitioners, rebirth occurs in the home of enlightened sages, surrounded by divine wisdom from childhood—an extraordinary spiritual blessing.

verses.text_sanskrit:
तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम् |
यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन || ४३ ||
verses.transliteration:
tatra taṃ buddhisaṃyogaṃ labhate paurvadehikam |
yatate ca tato bhūyaḥ saṃsiddhau kurunandana || 43 ||
verses.translation: There, in that new birth, one regains the spiritual intellect and consciousness accumulated in previous lives, and strives with even greater vigor for perfection, O descendant of Kuru!
verses.meaning: Spiritual muscle memory is immortal. Child prodigies and intuitive seekers are souls who awaken the spiritual insights of past lifetimes (Buddhi-samyogam paurva-dehikam) and pick up their journey right where they left off.

verses.text_sanskrit:
पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः |
जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते || ४४ ||
verses.transliteration:
pūrvābhyāsena tenaiva hriyate hyavaśo'pi saḥ |
jijñāsurapi yogasya śabdabrahmātivartate || 44 ||
verses.translation: By virtue of that past practice, one is helplessly and irresistibly drawn toward the spiritual path. Even a mere seeker who genuinely inquires into Yoga transcends the ritualistic realm of scriptural words (Shabda-Brahman).
verses.meaning: Past spiritual momentum acts as a divine gravitational pull. Even an initial, sincere curiosity about truth elevates a person beyond dry, ritualistic dogmas into living, transformative spiritual realization.

verses.text_sanskrit:
प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः |
अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम् || ४५ ||
verses.transliteration:
prayatnādyatamānastu yogī saṃśuddhakilbiṣaḥ |
anekajanmasaṃsiddhastato yāti parāṃ gatim || 45 ||
verses.translation: Striving with sincere and sustained effort, purified of all impurities, accumulating perfection over the course of many lifetimes (Aneka-janma-samsiddha), the yogi at last attains the Supreme Goal.
verses.meaning: Spiritual evolution is a magnificent multi-lifetime journey. Every prayer, meditation, and selfless act adds to the soul's momentum until, completely purified, it achieves the supreme summit of liberation.

verses.text_sanskrit:
तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः |
कर्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन || ४६ ||
verses.transliteration:
tapasvibhyo'dhiko yogī jñānibhyo'pi mato'dhikaḥ |
karmibhyaścādhiko yogī tasmādyogī bhavārjuna || 46 ||
verses.translation: The yogi is superior to the ascetic performing severe austerities; the yogi is superior even to the theoretical scholar of knowledge; and the yogi is superior to the ritualistic worker. Therefore, O Arjuna, be a yogi!
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna's glorious, resounding call to action: Integrated Yoga—unifying devotion, meditation, wisdom, and selfless action—surpasses dry asceticism, mere intellectual scholarship, and transactional rituals. 'Tasmad yogi bhavarjuna' — Therefore, become a yogi!

verses.text_sanskrit:
योगिनापि सर्वेषां मद्गतेनान्तरात्मना |
श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः || ४७ ||
verses.transliteration:
yogināmapi sarveṣāṃ madgatenāntarātmanā |
śraddhāvānbhajate yo māṃ sa me yuktatamo mataḥ || 47 ||
verses.translation: And of all yogis, one who with deep faith worships Me, with the inner self fully absorbed in Me—that person is considered by Me to be the most deeply united and foremost of all (Yuktatama).
verses.meaning: The crowning crescendo of Chapter 6: While all forms of Yoga are noble, the highest, most elevated yogi (Yuktatama) is one who loves and worships the Supreme Lord Sri Krishna with complete faith, total surrender, and an absorbed heart.
